page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance based on AMD processor technology and running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs paired with 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per core. Designed for high-throughput, data-intensive operational environments, it incorporates 23,038 GB of integrated local NVMe solid-state storage directly attached to the virtual host.

The defining architectural characteristic of the L96as_v5 is its massive local NVMe SSD capacity, which significantly reduces I/O access latencies compared to remote block storage. With 96 fully dedicated execution threads, compute operations avoid virtualization oversubscription penalties. The instance includes no discrete graphical accelerators, maintaining a GPU count of zero. Additionally, standard provisioning includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard Azure network routing configurations for external connectivity.

From a resource and cost efficiency perspective, bundling over 23 TB of fast local flash storage with 768 GB of memory allows heavy consolidation of data infrastructure into a single node rather than multiple smaller instances. This setup provides strong hardware density for I/O-bound enterprise tasks, making it suited for large-scale transactional relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, data warehousing, and real-time big data analytics pipelines.
